name: calculator
description: Evaluate a basic arithmetic expression (+, -, *, /, **). Use this for numeric calculations, not for general reasoning.
when_to_call: Any request needing real arithmetic (comparisons, timelines, budgets) -- never let the LLM guess a calculation.

name: retrieve
description: Search the local knowledge base for information relevant to a query. Use this to ground answers in ingested documents rather than guessing.
when_to_call: When the user's question might be answered by something already indexed (via --index-file) -- grounds the answer instead of guessing.
example_response: [fixture_doc::c0 | source=fixture | score=3.0883] Kubernetes is a container orchestration platform for automating deployment and scaling.

name: calendar_day
description: Look up meetings, events, and scheduling conflicts for a given day.
when_to_call: Questions like 'what's on my calendar today' or 'do I have any scheduling conflicts' -- needs a real CalendarClient (OAuth-authenticated in production, not wired into this trace CLI).
example_response:
Events on 2026-01-15:
- 09:00-10:00 Sprint planning
- 09:30-10:00 1:1 with manager

1 scheduling conflict(s) detected.

name: github_activity
description: Fetch a summary of GitHub activity (commits, pull requests, issues) for a repository within a date range. Use this for questions like 'what did I accomplish on this project this week?'
when_to_call: Questions like 'what did I accomplish on this project this week' -- needs a real GitHubClient with a real API token (not wired into this trace CLI).
example_response:
Activity in owner/repo from 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-31:

Commits (1):
- 2026-01-10 [abc1234] Fix refund calculation bug

name: email_summary
description: Fetch and classify emails within a date range into FYI, action required, waiting for response, commitment, or urgent. Use this for questions like 'what important emails did I receive today?'
when_to_call: Questions like 'what important emails did I get today' -- needs a real EmailClient (not wired into this trace CLI) and makes a real Gemini call per email to classify it.

name: analyze_feedback
description: Analyze a list of raw customer/stakeholder feedback strings: clusters them into themes, estimates frequency/severity, flags critical issues, and recommends actions. Use this when the user gives you multiple pieces of feedback to make sense of, not for a single freeform question.
when_to_call: The user gives you multiple pieces of raw feedback to make sense of -- clusters into themes, estimates severity, recommends actions.
example_response: {"top_themes":[{"theme":"Slow Refunds","frequency":1,"severity":0.9,"customer_impact":"Customers experience prolonged wait times to receive their money back.","trend":"stable"},{"theme":"Unresponsive Support","frequency":1,"severity":1.0,"customer_impact":"Customers are left without assistance as support fails to respond.","trend":"stable"}],"emerging_themes":[],"declining_themes":[],"critical_issues":["Complete lack of response from customer support","Excessive delays in processing refunds"],"recommended_actions":["Investigate and resolve the bottleneck in refund processing times","Audit customer support queue management to address unresponded tickets"]}

name: analyze_jd
description: Analyze a job description against the candidate's own retrieved resume/achievement documents: fit scores, major gaps, recommended resume changes, interview risks. Requires documents to already be indexed (e.g. via --index-file) -- returns an error if none are available. Use this when the user pastes a job description and asks about fit.
when_to_call: The user pastes a job description and asks about fit -- requires documents already indexed (e.g. via --index-file); returns an error otherwise.

example_request.jd_text: Senior Product Manager, requires 3+ years PM experience and cross-functional leadership.

example_response: {"overall_fit":0.5,"technical_fit":0.0,"ai_fit":0.0,"pm_fit":0.7,"domain_fit":0.0,"leadership_fit":0.8,"major_gaps":["No explicit mention of general product management methodology or years of experience meeting the senior seniority signal."],"recommended_resume_changes":["Explicitly highlight the title or role of 'Product Manager' in the resume excerpt to directly match the required skill of product management."],"interview_risks":["The candidate's experience is limited to a single project leading a small team of 6, which may raise questions about meeting the full scope of a 'Senior Product Manager' role."]}

name: draft_prd
description: Draft a PRD (problem statement, customer context, hypothesis, solution, metrics, experiment) for a product idea, grounded in retrieved existing product docs when available. Requires documents to already be indexed (e.g. via --index-file) -- works with no context if none are indexed, just without grounding. Use this when the user describes a product idea and asks for a PRD, not for general product-strategy questions.
when_to_call: The user describes a product idea and asks for a PRD -- requires documents already indexed to ground context; works without grounding if none indexed.

example_request.idea: Automate refund status notifications for customers.

example_response: {"problem_statement":"Customers lack automated visibility into the status of their refunds, leading to uncertainty and potential support inquiries following the self-serve refund flow.","customer_context":"Customers who utilize the self-serve refund flow (which reduced average refund resolution time from 5 days to 8 hours).","hypothesis":"If we automate refund status notifications for customers, then customer anxiety and support overhead will decrease because they will have real-time visibility into their refund progress.","solution":"Automated notification system that sends status updates to customers throughout the refund lifecycle.","metrics":["Reduction in refund-related support tickets","Customer satisfaction (CSAT) score for the refund experience"],"experiment":"Send manual status update emails for a cohort of refund requests and measure the impact on support ticket volume compared to a control group before building full automation."}
